page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7se.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at a base frequency of 2.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place the ecs.g7se.2xlarge consistently in the average tier across multiple workloads. The Intel Xeon processor delivers a single-core stress-ng score of 1858.18 and a multi-core score of 7750.15. Memory bandwidth is measured at 422.95 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 58.09 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. In application-specific tests, the instance achieves a static web serving throughput of 11.25 GB/sec and handles 7.88 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. However, the lack of GPU acceleration limits its utility for larger artificial intelligence tasks, as demonstrated by a weak text generation speed of 6.62 tokens per second on a 7B parameter language model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced resource profile offer a stable foundation for standard enterprise applications without the premium associated with specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. The absence of bundled local storage means storage costs are decoupled, allowing users to scale network storage independently. This instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, software compilation, database operations, and lightweight text or image processing tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7se.2xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.9 GHz, it features 4 physical cores with hyper-threading. The instance does not include local SSD storage or GPU accelerators, relying on a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data indicates average performance across standard compute and memory tasks, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 5658.0 and a static web serving throughput of 11.25 GB/sec. While it exhibits weak performance on medium-sized language model inference due to the lack of hardware acceleration, it delivers reliable, balanced throughput for standard enterprise workloads. It is highly suitable for web serving, software compilation, database operations, and general-purpose application hosting.
